claim: Many-pair translating telephones and speech-to-speech translation are commonly used (2009; restated for common language pairs in 2019)
originalWording: Many-pair translating telephones and speech-to-speech translation are commonly used (2009; restated for common language pairs in 2019)

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Live two-way speech-to-speech translation is built into ordinary phone calls and commonly used across many language pairs.
strict.rationale: In 2009 only narrow apps such as Jibbigo (English–Spanish) existed. Native in-call spoken translation finally shipped in Apple's iOS 26 in September 2025 for a handful of major language pairs on supported iPhones, which is real progress but not yet established as commonly used across many language pairs worldwide.
changedConditions: Enforces native telephone-call integration and common adoption rather than standalone app availability

evidence.title: How do you say? — Carnegie Mellon on Jibbigo
evidence.note: Fall 2009 university account of English–Spanish speech translation on iPhone. Not evidence of common use across many language pairs.

evidence.title: Start a conversation with Google
evidence.note: Speech conversation mode expanded to 14 languages; still described as alpha. Not equivalent to translation quality or universal adoption.

evidence.title: Google Translate: 2015 official product updates
evidence.note: Conversation and speech translation documented in product updates. Text-language counts must not be presented as speech-language counts; 44-language wearable speech support is separately identified.

evidence.title: Apple: Live Translation shipping in iOS 26
evidence.note: Shipping real-time spoken translation in Phone for selected language pairs; five languages at initial launch. Not every language, country or device.

evidence.title: Apple: Translate phone calls and conversations
evidence.note: Current iOS 26 guide lists one-on-one spoken Phone translation across English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese and Korean variants. Supports actual telephone integration, not perfect translation quality.

reference.criterion: Ordinary users have practical two-way spoken translation for many language pairs; no perfect all-language requirement.
reference.rationale: Jibbigo provided a real but limited 2009 translating-phone capability. It was not yet a routine many-pair service. Google’s 2011 and 2015 conversation/speech products establish the broader consumer capability by 2015. Accents and mistakes do not negate ordinary practical use.
